name: Natufian
material_culture_traits: stone tools, sickle blades, mortars
description: Semi-sedentary hunter-gatherers of the Levant, among the earliest to cultivate wild cereals.

name: Pre-Pottery Neolithic A
material_culture_traits: monumental architecture, early cultivation
description: Earliest Neolithic culture in the Levant with monumental architecture at Jericho.

name: Pre-Pottery Neolithic B
material_culture_traits: rectangular mud-brick houses, long-distance obsidian trade
description: Expansion of farming communities across the Fertile Crescent with long-distance trade networks.

name: Catalhoyuk Culture
material_culture_traits: wall paintings, bull symbolism, obsidian tools
description: One of the earliest proto-urban settlements with rich symbolic art and dense habitation.

name: Yangshao
material_culture_traits: painted ceramics, stone tools, silk production
description: Major Neolithic culture of northern China known for distinctive painted pottery.

name: Longshan
material_culture_traits: walled settlements, jade working, scapulimancy
description: Late Neolithic culture showing early social stratification and proto-urban development.

name: Vinca
pottery_style: dark burnished pottery with incised designs
material_culture_traits: Vinca symbols (possible proto-writing), copper smelting, figurines
description: Major Neolithic-Chalcolithic culture of southeastern Europe with early copper metallurgy and enigmatic symbols.

name: Cucuteni-Trypillia
material_culture_traits: mega-settlements (up to 15,000 people), ritual house burning, figurines
description: Created some of the largest settlements in the world at the time, with elaborate painted ceramics.

name: Yamnaya
material_culture_traits: wagons, horse domestication, kurgan burials
description: Steppe pastoralists strongly associated with the spread of Proto-Indo-European languages across Europe.

name: Corded Ware
material_culture_traits: battle axes, cord-decorated beakers, single-grave tradition
description: Widespread European culture linked to Indo-European expansion from the steppe.

name: Bell Beaker
burial_practices: individual burials with standardized grave goods
material_culture_traits: copper daggers, archery equipment, gold ornaments
description: Pan-European phenomenon associated with the spread of metallurgy and possibly Celtic/Italic languages.

name: Clovis
material_culture_traits: distinctive fluted projectile points, megafauna hunting
description: Earliest widespread culture in the Americas, known for distinctive fluted spear points.

name: Folsom
material_culture_traits: finely fluted points (smaller than Clovis), bison hunting specialization
description: Successor to Clovis, specialized in bison hunting on the Great Plains.

name: Jomon
material_culture_traits: cord-marked pottery, lacquerware, dogu figurines
description: One of the world's earliest pottery-making cultures with a sophisticated hunter-gatherer economy lasting over 13,000 years.

name: Lapita
material_culture_traits: distinctive pottery, obsidian tools, shell ornaments
description: Ancestral culture of Polynesian, Melanesian, and Micronesian peoples, known for long-distance oceanic voyaging.

name: Mehrgarh
material_culture_traits: mud-brick architecture, dental drilling, cotton cultivation
description: One of the earliest farming communities in South Asia, precursor to the Indus Valley Civilization.

name: Indus Valley (Harappan)
material_culture_traits: urban planning, standardized weights, undeciphered script, sewage systems
description: Major Bronze Age civilization with sophisticated urban planning, writing, and trade networks.

name: Nok
material_culture_traits: terracotta sculptures, early iron smelting
description: Known for remarkable terracotta sculptures and early iron smelting in sub-Saharan Africa.

name: Olmec
material_culture_traits: colossal stone heads, jade working, early writing, ball game
description: Mother culture of Mesoamerica, creators of the colossal basalt heads and early writing systems.

name: Linear Pottery (LBK)
material_culture_traits: longhouses, polished stone tools, Spondylus shell ornaments
description: First farming culture to colonize Central Europe from the Balkans, bringing Neolithic agriculture.

name: Funnel Beaker (TRB)
material_culture_traits: megaliths, amber trade, cattle-based economy
description: Northern European Neolithic culture responsible for building many of the region's megalithic tombs.

name: Caral-Supe
material_culture_traits: monumental pyramids, quipu (knotted strings), no ceramics
description: One of the oldest urban centers in the Americas, contemporary with Egyptian pyramids but without pottery or writing.

name: Ubaid
material_culture_traits: irrigation canals, multi-room mud-brick houses, early temples
description: Proto-urban culture of southern Mesopotamia that laid the foundations for Sumerian civilization.

name: Uruk
material_culture_traits: earliest writing (cuneiform), cylinder seals, monumental temples
description: World's first urban civilization, birthplace of writing and complex bureaucracy.

name: Gobekli Tepe Builders
material_culture_traits: monumental carved T-shaped pillars, animal reliefs
description: Builders of the world's oldest known monumental architecture, predating agriculture.

name: Kerma
burial_practices: massive tumulus burials with sacrificial retainers
material_culture_traits: monumental mud-brick architecture (deffufa), bronze working
description: Major Nubian kingdom contemporary with and rival to Egypt's Middle Kingdom.

name: Ban Chiang
burial_practices: burials with pottery and bronze goods
material_culture_traits: early bronze working, painted pottery, rice cultivation
description: Important prehistoric site demonstrating early metallurgy and rice cultivation in Southeast Asia.
